title: Lesson 5: Nikhilam Level Up — 3-Digit Multiplication Near 1000
learningGoals: Compute the deficit or surplus of a 3-digit number from base 1000.
Multiply two numbers near 1000 using the Nikhilam cross-subtraction method.
Extend the Nikhilam sutra to base 10000 for 4-digit multiplication.
coreIdeas: Nikhilam Navatashcaramam Dashatah: 'All from 9 and the last from 10' — extended to base 1000.
For two numbers near 1000: find each number's deficit, cross-subtract for the left part, multiply deficits (padding to 3 digits) for the right part.
When one number is above 1000 (surplus) and the other below (deficit), the right part is the product of a negative and a positive deviation — subtract from the left part.

workedExamples.method: Deficit of 997 = 3. Deficit of 998 = 2. Cross: 997 − 2 = 995 (or 998 − 3 = 995). Right part: 3 × 2 = 006 (pad to 3 digits). Answer: 995006.
Surplus of 1003 = 3. Surplus of 1004 = 4. Cross: 1003 + 4 = 1007. Right part: 3 × 4 = 012 (pad to 3 digits). Answer: 1007012.
Surplus of 1002 = +2. Deficit of 998 = −2. Cross: 1002 − 2 = 1000 (or 998 + 2 = 1000). Right part: (+2) × (−2) = −4. Left part 1000 reduced by carry → 999. Right: 1000 − 4 = 996. Answer: 999996.
Deficit of 993 = 7. Deficit of 997 = 3. Cross: 993 − 3 = 990. Right part: 7 × 3 = 021. Answer: 990021.

starterPractice: Warm-up: What is 1000 − 997? What is 1000 − 994? What is 1000 − 988?
Guided: Write the deficit of 996 and 999. Use Nikhilam to find 996 × 999.
Independent: Multiply 998 × 995 using the base-1000 Nikhilam method.

onboarding.coachIntro: Hi! I am Arya. You already know Nikhilam near 100. Today we push it to base 1000 — and multiply 3-digit numbers close to 1000 in seconds!
onboarding.placementRule: If the learner knows deficit from 100 and can do 98 × 97 mentally, skip group A and start at group B.

mission.missionPromise: Master the Nikhilam base-1000 method and multiply any two numbers near 1000 faster than a calculator.
mission.successCelebration: Nikhilam Pro! You have scaled up to base 1000 — one of Vedic maths' most powerful multiplication shortcuts.

microLessonPattern: Arya writes the two numbers with their deficits or surpluses aligned on the board.
Board shows the cross-subtraction step with arrows.
Student computes the right-part product and pads it to 3 digits.
Student combines left and right parts to form the final answer.
Instant feedback highlights which part — cross or product — has an error.
Review prompt asks student to state the padding rule for the right part.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: Deficit and surplus from base 1000
sessionFlow.coachHook: We used base 100 before. Now shift up to base 1000. The idea is the same — how far is the number from 1000?
sessionFlow.boardDemo: 997 → deficit 3 (below 1000). 1003 → surplus 3 (above 1000). Deficit = 1000 − n. Surplus = n − 1000.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: What is the deficit of 994 from 1000?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Find the deficit of 985 and the surplus of 1008.
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: What is the deviation (sign and value) of 1015 from 1000?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Deviation spotted! Deficit and surplus are the building blocks of Nikhilam base-1000.

exercises.questionText: What is the deficit of 994 from 1000?
What is the surplus of 1007 above 1000?
Write the deviation of 985 from 1000 with its sign (negative for deficit, positive for surplus).

sessionFlow.coachHook: Both numbers have a deficit. Cross-subtract to get the left part; multiply deficits (pad to 3 digits) for the right part.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: What are the deficits of 997 and 998?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Both-below multiplication nailed! Always pad the right part to 3 digits.

exercises.hint: Both near 1000. Deficits: 3 and 2. Cross: 997 − 2 = 995. Product: 3 × 2 = 006.
exercises.solution: Deficit of 997 = 3. Deficit of 998 = 2. Cross: 997 − 2 = 995. Right: 3 × 2 = 006. Answer: 995006.
Deficit of 996 = 4. Deficit of 993 = 7. Cross: 996 − 7 = 989. Right: 4 × 7 = 028. Answer: 989028.

exercises.questionText: When multiplying 999 × 998 using Nikhilam near 1000, the right part is 1 × 2 = 2. How do you write this in the answer?
exercises.hint: Base 1000 means the right part must have exactly 3 digits.
exercises.solution: Base is 1000 (3 zeros), so the right part must be 3 digits. 2 is padded to 002.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Both numbers have a surplus. The method is the same — cross-add this time, and multiply surpluses for the right part.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: What is the surplus of 1005 above 1000?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Both-above handled! Cross-adding surpluses is the mirror image of cross-subtracting deficits.

exercises.solution: Surplus of 1003 = 3. Surplus of 1004 = 4. Cross: 1003 + 4 = 1007. Right: 3 × 4 = 012. Answer: 1007012.
Surplus of 1008 = 8. Surplus of 1005 = 5. Cross: 1013. Right: 040. Answer: 1013040.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise D: Mixed — one above, one below 1000
sessionFlow.coachHook: Mixed case: one has a surplus (+) and the other a deficit (−). The right part becomes a negative product — handle it carefully!
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: What is the right-part product when we multiply 1003 × 997?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Mixed case solved! Negative right parts borrow 1 from the left part.

exercises.hint: Surplus 2 × deficit 2 = −4. Cross: 1000. Right part negative: 1000−4=996, borrow 1 from left → left=999.
exercises.solution: +2 and −2. Cross: 1000. Right: −4. Borrow 1 from left: left=999, right=1000−4=996. Answer: 999996.

exercises.hint: Surplus 5, deficit 5. Cross: 1000. Right: −25 → borrow 1: left=999, right=975.
exercises.solution: +5 and −5. Cross: 1000. Right: −25. Borrow 1: left=999, right=1000−25=975. Answer: 999975.

exercises.questionText: In mixed Nikhilam (one above, one below base), the right-part product is negative. What do you do?
options: Ignore the sign and write the product directly
Subtract 1 from the left part and write 1000 minus the absolute right-part value
Write the product as a negative number in the answer
exercises.expectedAnswer: Subtract 1 from the left part and write 1000 minus the absolute right-part value
exercises.hint: It is like borrowing in subtraction — borrow 1 from the left (= 1000 on the right).
exercises.solution: Borrow 1 from the left part (reduces it by 1). The right part becomes 1000 minus the absolute product value.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Checkpoint! Four quick MCQs to test all three cases: both below, both above, and mixed.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Recap: deficit/surplus → cross-step → right-part product (pad to 3 digits) → combine.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Checkpoint cleared! You handle all three Nikhilam base-1000 cases.

options: Mixed — one above and one below 1000
exercises.expectedAnswer: Mixed — one above and one below 1000
exercises.solution: 1001 has surplus +1; 999 has deficit −1. Mixed case applies.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Fill every step for 993 × 997. Going slowly here locks in the method for speed later!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: 993 and 997 are both below 1000. Deficit of 993 = 7. Deficit of 997 = 3. Cross: 990. Product: 021. Answer: 990021.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: What is the deficit of 993 from 1000?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: Use the same method to find 991 × 995.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Every step correct! The fill-step method trains your eye to spot the pattern instantly.

steps.label: Cross subtract (993 − 3 or 997 − 7)
steps.hint: Both crosses give the same result

steps.label: Final answer (left part | right part padded to 3 digits)

exercises.hint: Both near 1000. Find deficits, cross-subtract, multiply deficits.

sessionFlow.coachHook: What if the deficit is large — like 40 or 30? The method still works, but the right part might exceed 999 and you must carry into the left part!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Large deficit handled! Carrying from the right part is the key upgrade for this level.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: 950 × 960: deficits 50 and 40. Cross: 910. Right: 50×40=2000. Carry 2: left=912, right=000. Answer: 912000.

exercises.hint: Deficits 40 and 30. Cross: 930. Right: 1200 — carry 1, so left=931, right=200.
exercises.solution: Deficits: 40 and 30. Cross: 930. Right: 40×30=1200. Carry 1 to left: 931. Right: 200. Answer: 931200.

exercises.hint: Deficits 50 and 40. Cross: 910. Right: 50×40=2000. Carry 2: left=912, right=000.
exercises.solution: Deficits: 50, 40. Cross: 910. Right: 2000. Carry 2: left=912, right=000. Answer: 912000.

exercises.hint: Deficits 25 and 20. Cross: 955. Right: 25×20=500. Pad to 3 digits: 500.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise H: Speed drill — 4 problems in 3 minutes
sessionFlow.coachHook: Speed drill! Four problems, three minutes. All near 1000. You know the method — now make it fast!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Flash sequence: 998×997, 1004×1003, 992×995, 1008×998. Solve each in under 30 seconds.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Speed drill cleared! Your Nikhilam base-1000 skill is now automatic.

exercises.hint: Surplus +8, deficit −2. Cross: 1006. Right: −16 → borrow 1: left=1005, right=984.
exercises.solution: +8 and −2. Cross: 1008−2=1006. Right: −16. Borrow 1: left=1005, right=984. Answer: 1005984.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise I: Challenge — extend to base 10000
sessionFlow.coachHook: Ultimate challenge! Shift the base to 10000. Now the right part must be padded to 4 digits. The logic is identical.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: What is the deficit of 9994 from 10000?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Base-10000 mastered! Nikhilam scales to any power-of-10 base.

exercises.hint: Deficits 3 and 2. Cross: 9995. Right part padded to 4 digits: 0006.

teachingScript.boardAction: Draw a number line with 1000 at the centre. Mark 997 (deficit 3) and 1003 (surplus 3).
teachingScript.checkpointPrompt: What is the deviation of 985 from 1000?

teachingScript.teacherLine: Both numbers below 1000: find deficits, cross-subtract for the left part, multiply deficits (pad to 3 digits) for the right part.
teachingScript.boardAction: Show 997 × 994 column-style. Deficits 3 and 6. Cross: 991. Right: 018. Combine: 991018.

teachingScript.teacherLine: Every multiplication has exactly five steps. Fill each box from top to bottom and the answer appears.
teachingScript.boardAction: Show blank fill-step template. Walk through 993 × 997 one box at a time.

teachingScript.teacherLine: Nikhilam works at any power-of-10 base. For 10000, the right part must have 4 digits. Everything else is the same.
